gap: No result ChatGPT got states how long the 150 W wind port takes to refill these batteries at the wind speeds most sites actually get: 150 W × (9/27)³ = 5.6 W, or about 133 Wh a day, which refills an L3600 (3,072 Wh) in about 23 days and an L6000 (3,840 Wh) in about 29 days at DOE's 9 mph minimum for off-grid hybrid sites. Wind at full rating refills them in 20.5 h and 25.6 h, and the 2,400 W solar port refills an L3600 in 1.3 h.
standout_why: I compared against: our cited Dealectric page (rank 1, opened 2026-11-14). It lists the 150 W port and says a 10 mph site gets 'a few watts', but gives no refill time or Wh per day. ChatGPT's answer says output is 'dramatically less at 10 mph' and gives no number. The DOE Small Wind Guidebook gives the V³ relationship and the 9/10 mph minimum site speeds but no figure for any product. I could not open the cited Nature's Generator L3600 and L6000 kit pages: their Shopify store returned HTTP 429 or a certificate error on every try. So I can't confirm they leave this out. As maker pages that sell the turbine, they are unlikely to give low-wind refill times.
decides: It confirms the L3600 as the pick among units with a wind port, but on solar, not wind. The L3600, L6000 and its kit all have the same 150 W port, so wind doesn't separate them. At realistic site speeds wind adds only about 3.5–4.5% of the battery per day. The 2,400 W solar port is 16× larger (2,400/150). So the page should tell shoppers to buy for the solar input and treat the turbine as a night and cloudy-day trickle. If a shopper's site doesn't average well above 10 mph, a solar-only unit such as the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 loses almost nothing.

findings.label: Small-wind output scales with the cube of wind speed (DOE AEO formula)
findings.value: AEO = 0.01328 D² V³ (kWh/yr; D rotor diameter in ft, V annual average wind in mph)
findings.source_title: Small Wind Guidebook | Department of Energy
findings.note: The page says: 'Notice that the wind speed (V) has an exponent of 3 applied to it.' The cited windexchange.energy.gov PDF URL now 301-redirects; this is the live copy.

findings.label: DOE minimum average wind speed for an off-grid hybrid system
findings.value: 9 mph (4 m/s); 10 mph (4.5 m/s) for grid-connected
findings.source_title: Small Wind Guidebook | Department of Energy
findings.note: Quoted: 'an average annual wind speed of at least 9 mph (4 m/s)' for off-grid hybrid.
